newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNI FOCUS - prices flat in pre-holiday mode.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNI FOCUS - prices flat in pre-holiday mode.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices opened mostly flat as the market began to downshift ahead of the Memorial Day weekend.
Early Thursday activity amounted to "absolutely nothing," with a single bid list totaling $20 million to $30 million in circulation, one trader said.
"I have a feeling that we are going to shift in to Memorial Day weekend mode pretty soon here," the trader said.

Though he judged muni cash unchanged, the trader said players were a bit tentative after Wednesday's session, which marked "the first down day you had in a while." The supply picture, however, remains "very managable," he said.
"Our market is in decent shape," the trader said.
A second trader expects municipals to drift lower Thursday and Friday as players lighten positions ahead of the holiday, he said.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended a 1400 EDT close Friday for U.S. Treasuries and related markets, and a full close for Monday.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 4/32 at 95-21/32 to yield 6.97 percent. In debt futures, the June Municipal contract was up 3/32 at 116-9/32. The June T-bond contract was up 1/32 at 109-10/32. The MOB spread was 223 ticks.
On the economic front, U.S. jobless claims for the week ended May 17 rose to 322,000 versus average estimates for 324,000, and against the prior week's downwardly revised 317,000.
Thursday's municipal bond offerings are expected to total $580 million in 23 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings are expected to total $353 million in seven sales, with a $209 million Metropolitian Washington Airport, D.C., deal through Lehman Brothers topping the list. On the competitive side, 16 sales totaling $227 million are scheduled. A $160 million Florida issue at 1100 EDT is the largest.
